prompt_turn0:
You are playing Missile Command. Enemy missiles are falling towards a line of positions numbered 0 to 9. Your cities sit at fixed positions on that line and each threat line tells you the position where that missile will land and the tick it lands on. A missile that lands on a city destroys it. A missile that lands on empty ground does nothing at all, so a threat you leave alone may cost you nothing.

You have silos on their own fixed positions, each holding a limited number of interceptors, and a silo can only reach a landing position within four of its own position. Each turn you may fire one interceptor from one silo at one threat, or you may fire nothing. Interceptors are scarce: spending one on a threat that could not have hurt you means it is not there when a city needs it. Every turn the tick advances by one, and any missile whose landing tick has arrived lands.

tick 0
city A at 2
silo 1 at 2 ammo 1
threat P impact 2 tick 2

The actions you have already taken are: none yet

Answer with exactly two characters: the number of the silo first, then the letter of the threat. 3W would mean fire from silo 3 at a threat called W -- no silo 3 and no threat W exist here, that is only the shape of an answer. If you want to fire nothing this turn, answer with the single word PASS. You may add an explanation after your answer, and it will be ignored.

ended_why: every threat has been resolved by tick 2
missing_values_are_not_tokens: a missing value is never passed to the simulator, so it can never be scored as a wrong move -- the empty-list rule
unreadable_is_a_simulator_outcome: `malformed` is the simulator's own outcome for a token that is not an action: COUNTED, NEVER SCORED AS A WRONG MOVE -- the board is unchanged and the tick advances. `unknown`, `late`, `out_of_range` and `no_ammo` are four DIFFERENT claims and are never merged into it.

protocol.clock: the state's own `tick` integer, advanced one per action
protocol.interface_decision: turn-based BY CONSTRUCTION -- missile_command.py carries no wall-clock term, so no frozen criterion was changed to make it turn-based (see clock_audit)

clock_audit.reading: NO WALL-CLOCK TERM EXISTS IN THE FROZEN SIMULATOR -- the play mode is turn-based by construction, so step-locking the clock is not a change this cabinet could make: there is nothing to lock. The only clock is the state's own `tick` integer, advanced one per action.
